easy.q: According to Elder Andersen, what does our faith in Jesus Christ give us?
options: Courage to choose the right
A life with no hard days
Quick answers to every question
easy.why: Elder Andersen taught that as we choose faith in Christ, He blesses us with courage to choose the right, even in very difficult situations.

easy.q: When Elder Andersen was a boy on a dairy farm, what did he do on summer mornings after milking?
options: Rode his horse and guided the cows to a high meadow
Drove a tractor out to plow the far fields
Walked the sheep down to drink at the river
easy.why: He spent all day with the cows, alone with his thoughts, and taught, “We need stillness to nourish our faith in Christ.”

easy.q: Moroni was alone, without family or friends. What did he bravely declare?
options: He would travel to find a new people
He would not deny the Christ
He would stop writing on the plates
easy.why: Elder Andersen quoted Moroni’s words, “And I, Moroni, will not deny the Christ,” as an example of spiritual courage born of faith.

easy.q: After fires destroyed their neighborhood, what did Cody and Haylee Woodbury tell Elder Andersen?
options: They planned to move to another state
They wished they had left much sooner
Their family was safe and their faith secure
easy.why: They said, “We can build another house.” Elder Andersen said their faith in Jesus Christ lifted their courage.

easy.q: How did 17-year-old Rosemary Chibota first learn that the gospel was true?
options: She heard a choir sing at a Church meeting
She read a pamphlet about Joseph Smith
She visited a temple with her parents
easy.why: She read a Joseph Smith pamphlet missionaries had left at her home in Zimbabwe and received a spiritual witness that it was true.

medium.q: Why did Elder Andersen describe his long days alone with the cows, with no phone or music?
options: To show that farm life is better than city life
To teach that we need stillness to nourish our faith
To explain how he learned to care for animals
To suggest that young people should not own phones
medium.why: He said, “Times have changed, but our spirits have not changed. We need stillness to nourish our faith in Christ.”

medium.q: How did Elder Andersen describe the way faith in Christ and courage work together?
options: Courage must come first, and faith follows much later
Faith removes any need for us to have courage
Faith brings courage, and using that courage strengthens faith
They are two different names for the very same gift
medium.why: He taught that Christ blesses those who choose faith with courage to choose the right, and that as we show that courage, “our faith in Christ strengthens.”

medium.q: Elder Andersen quoted Paul: “We wrestle not against flesh and blood.” What did he say these words describe?
options: The physical dangers Moroni faced from his enemies
The hard daily labor of life on a small farm
The disagreements that arise among neighbors
The doubts, distractions, and deceptions of our day
medium.why: Elder Andersen said our world differs from Moroni’s, but discipleship still requires courage against today’s doubts, distractions, and deceptions.

medium.q: What did Elder Andersen say we are given in quiet moments when we pray privately to Heavenly Father?
options: Increased courage to choose the right
Quick relief from all of our trials
Knowledge of what others should change
Freedom from ever needing to pray again
medium.why: He taught that faith gives us the desire to kneel alone and pray, and in those quiet moments we receive increased courage to choose the right.

medium.q: After telling how Peter and John answered the rulers, what did Elder Andersen do “as Peter and John of old”?
options: He promised that the sick among us will be healed
He called on the rulers of nations to believe
He bore his own witness that Jesus Christ lives
He invited us to study the Acts of the Apostles
medium.why: Peter and John declared the name of Jesus Christ with courage born of their faith. Elder Andersen then added his own witness: “He lives. He guides this holy work.”

hard.q: Which statement best matches Elder Andersen’s definition of spiritual courage?
options: Feeling no doubt or fear when it is time to choose the right
Triumphing over obstacles, doubt, and fear in choosing the right
Defending our beliefs forcefully whenever they are challenged
Facing physical danger without ever thinking of turning back
hard.why: He defined spiritual courage as “the triumph over obstacles, doubt, and fear in choosing the right.” It overcomes doubt and fear rather than never feeling them.

hard.q: In this talk, why is a young mother preparing her small children for church an example of remarkable courage?
options: She goes knowing some Sundays will be more struggle than renewal
She goes because each Sunday always leaves her feeling renewed
She goes only on the weeks when her children are well behaved
She goes mainly so that other members will notice her effort
hard.why: Elder Andersen said she acts with faith, “knowing that some Sundays will be more a wrestle of survival than a spiritual renewal.”

hard.q: Elder Andersen quoted Paul: “troubled on every side, yet not distressed.” What did he use these words to teach?
options: True disciples are spared from life’s hardest challenges
Challenges are a sign that our faith has grown weak
With hope alive in Christ, we can face challenges without despair
Hope returns only after life’s challenges have ended
hard.why: He said that with our hope alive in Christ, “even with life’s challenges,” we may be troubled and perplexed, yet not in despair.

hard.q: Which person best fits the promise Elder Andersen gave near the end of his talk?
options: Sam sets the commandments aside until his answers have come
Sam expects that courage alone will bring him his answers
Sam believes his answers must come before his faith can grow
Sam keeps the commandments while still waiting for answers
hard.why: He promised that as you strengthen your faith “by believing and following Him and keeping His commandments, your answers will come.” Believing and obeying come first; the answers follow.

hard.q: Which situation best fits what Elder Andersen taught about accepting a calling from priesthood leaders?
options: A member waits to accept until she feels fully qualified to serve
A member accepts because his schedule has finally opened up
A member who feels inadequate and short on time accepts in faith
A member accepts in order to gain experience in leading others
hard.why: He taught that faith in Jesus Christ gives us courage to accept a calling “even when we feel inadequate or without sufficient time.”
